title: Contact your doctor or maternity team promptly
intro: Some concerns need advice before the next routine appointment even when they do not feel like an emergency. If a symptom becomes severe, sudden or frightening, use urgent care instead.

signs.title: A symptom persists or keeps worsening
signs.detail: Contact care when pain, nausea, reflux, constipation, itching, swelling or another change is not settling or is disrupting eating, drinking, sleep, walking or daily life.

signs.title: You cannot manage food or fluids normally
signs.detail: Ask for help when vomiting continues, fluids are difficult to keep down, urination becomes much less frequent or you feel increasingly weak.

signs.title: You feel unwell or may have an infection
signs.detail: New feverishness, a concerning rash, painful urination, worsening cough or a significant infectious exposure deserves pregnancy-specific advice.

signs.title: Your mood or anxiety is affecting daily life
signs.detail: Tell a health professional when fear, low mood, panic, intrusive thoughts or poor sleep make it hard to function or care for yourself.

signs.title: You need to change a medicine or treatment
signs.detail: Review the exact prescription, painkiller, cold remedy, supplement, cream or treatment before starting, stopping or changing it.

signs.title: You feel unsafe, controlled or pressured
signs.detail: Ask to speak with a health professional privately. If there is immediate danger, use emergency help rather than waiting for an appointment.

action: Use the pregnancy or maternity contact route you were given and explain what changed, when it began and whether it is worsening. Escalate immediately if you feel in danger.

title: Urgent signs during pregnancy or within a year after birth
intro: Get medical care immediately for these symptoms. The list is not exhaustive; if something feels seriously wrong, seek help.

signs.title: A headache that will not go away
signs.detail: Especially if it worsens, feels unusually severe or comes with vision changes or marked swelling.

signs.title: Dizziness or fainting
signs.detail: New, repeated or severe dizziness, confusion, disorientation or loss of consciousness.

signs.title: Changes in vision
signs.detail: Flashes, blind spots, blurring, double vision or loss of vision.

signs.title: Fever
signs.detail: A temperature at or above the urgent threshold given by your local maternity service.

signs.title: Trouble breathing
signs.detail: Difficulty catching your breath, speaking and breathing, or breathing when lying down.

signs.title: Chest pain or a fast-beating heart
signs.detail: Pressure, pain, palpitations or an irregular heartbeat, especially with dizziness or breathlessness.

signs.title: Severe nausea and vomiting
signs.detail: You cannot keep fluids down, are urinating very little, feel confused, faint or dehydrated.

signs.title: Severe belly pain
signs.detail: Sudden, sharp, worsening or persistent abdominal pain, or pain reaching the shoulder, chest or back.

signs.title: Baby movement stops or slows
signs.detail: A clear change from your baby's usual movement pattern during pregnancy.

signs.title: Bleeding or fluid leaking during pregnancy
signs.detail: Bleeding heavier than spotting, a gush or trickle of fluid, or bad-smelling discharge.

signs.title: Heavy bleeding or abnormal discharge after birth
signs.detail: Rapidly soaking pads, large clots, tissue, bad-smelling discharge, weakness or faintness.

signs.title: Severe swelling, redness or pain in one limb
signs.detail: Especially a painful, warm or swollen calf, leg or arm on one side.

signs.title: Extreme swelling of hands or face
signs.detail: Sudden or marked swelling, especially with headache or vision changes.

signs.title: Overwhelming exhaustion
signs.detail: A sudden or extreme inability to function that is not relieved by rest.

signs.title: Thoughts of harming yourself or the baby
signs.detail: Or severe confusion, hallucinations, agitation or loss of contact with reality.

action: Call the emergency number for your region or go to an emergency department. Say that you are pregnant or were pregnant within the last year.

title: Urgent signs in a newborn or young baby
intro: Young babies can become unwell quickly. Contact urgent medical care if you notice these signs or are seriously worried.

signs.title: Breathing difficulty
signs.detail: Grunting, chest pulling in, pauses, very fast breathing, struggling to feed because of breathing or blue/grey color.

signs.title: Hard to wake or unusually floppy
signs.detail: Very low activity, poor responsiveness, weak movement or a marked change in alertness.

signs.title: Stopped feeding well
signs.detail: Refusing feeds, repeatedly unable to feed, choking with feeds or a clear drop from the baby's pattern.

signs.title: Abnormal temperature
signs.detail: Fever or low temperature according to the urgent threshold and measurement method given by local care.

signs.title: Seizure or unusual repetitive movements
signs.detail: Jerking that does not stop when held, stiffening, unusual eye movements or loss of responsiveness.

signs.title: Jaundice that needs prompt review
signs.detail: Yellow color in the first day, deepening yellow, yellow palms or soles, or jaundice with sleepiness or poor feeding.

signs.title: Signs of dehydration
signs.detail: Markedly fewer wet nappies, very dry mouth, a sunken soft spot, unusual sleepiness or poor feeding.

signs.title: A serious change that worries you
signs.detail: A weak or unusual cry, persistent vomiting, a new rash that does not fade under pressure, or simply seeming very unwell.

action: Use your baby's urgent care route or local emergency service now. Do not wait for a routine appointment when a young baby seems seriously unwell.
